comparison_note: All comparisons use completed days: yesterday (2026-08-03) is the run_date. Today is excluded as it is an incomplete day. Cell C Recharges compares yesterday against same-day-last-month and same-day-two-months-ago, plus MTD-vs-prior-MTD (same day-of-month cutoff, so periods are equal length). Note: 2026-08-03 is a Monday, 2026-07-03 a Friday, and 2026-06-03 a Wednesday — all weekdays this time, so the weekday/weekend mismatch that affected the previous run is less of a factor here.

flags: MTD recharge revenue (R838,743.89) is down 15.7% vs prior-MTD (R994,353.00), breaching the ±10% variance threshold. MTD count variance was 8.5% — within tolerance.
Same-day-last-month vs same-day-two-months-ago count varies 13.6% (21,391 vs 18,823), breaching the ±5% threshold.
Same-day-last-month vs same-day-two-months-ago value varies 21.0% (R350,470.00 vs R289,655.00), breaching the ±5% threshold.

Yesterday vs history did NOT breach the 20% drop rule this time: value was 80.0% of same-day-last-month (280,418 vs 350,470, just inside the 80% line) and 96.8% of same-day-two-months-ago; count was 87.2% and 99.0% respectively.

Revenue sanity check passed for all periods (AVG R14.89–R16.38). One single recharge of R14,876.00 on 2026-07-03 (and flowing into that month's MTD window) is well above the typical R2–R500 range but is diluted across 21,391+ records that day, keeping AVG normal (R16.38) — per policy this is not excluded, just noted for transparency.

Yesterday value dropped 23.0% vs same day last month (R294,454.26 vs R382,289.98), breaching the 20% threshold. Qty (down 19.2%) and both vs-two-months-ago comparisons (down 4.3% / 6.9%) stayed just inside the 20% line.
MTD vs prior-MTD variance breaches ±10% for both metrics: qty down 24.2% (71,523 vs 94,351), value down 50.5% (R1,013,265.28 vs R2,048,281.60).
Same-day-last-month vs same-day-two-months-ago variance breaches ±5% for both metrics: qty up 18.5%, value up 20.9%.
3-month trend abnormal on value: the prior-MTD → current-MTD leg moved -50.5%, well past the 25% single-leg threshold. The qty leg (-24.2%) came just under the 25% threshold and is not flagged.

Tenant breakdown for yesterday vs same-day-last-month shows the value decline is concentrated in uConnect (R288,840.71 → R376,070.02, -23.2%), while ME&YOU was comparatively stable (R5,613.55 → R6,219.96, -9.8%).

Revenue sanity check passed across all 9 days checked (Jun 1 – Aug 3) — AVG ranged R11.38–R34.53. One row on 2026-07-03 had a value of R12,261.28 (well above the normal per-account-day range) but is diluted across 28,330 rows that day and keeps AVG normal (R13.49); per policy this is not excluded. WhatsApp purchase columns excluded from all sums per known masking-policy artifact.
MTD Active-1 count among new subscribers dropped 74.1% vs prior-MTD (1,039 vs 4,016; rate 20.4% vs 45.0%), breaching the 60% threshold.

New-subscriber volume and new-subscriber Active-1 count both rose sharply vs the day before (2,149 vs 720 new subs; 401 vs 93 Active-1) — an increase, so the drop rule does not apply. Note new_subs_active1_day_before recomputed to 93 here vs 77 reported for the same 2026-08-02 date in yesterday's run: USAGE_0_30_DAYS is a live rolling flag on the base view, not a frozen historical snapshot, so counts for a past ACCOUNTCREATEDATE can shift slightly run to run as those accounts accrue more usage.
Day 2-4 registration-activity cohort (2,665) was 26.1% below the trailing 7-day average (3,607) — within the 60% tolerance, not flagged.

Day-30 Active-7 retention and never-used-vs-last-month comparisons remain N/A: the snapshot log has no entry for 2026-07-03 or 2026-06-03 yet (log currently covers 2026-07-21 onward plus 2026-08-02/03).

Spread between VW_ACTIVE_SUBSCRIPTIONS_USAGE_DETAILS (391,009) and the other two tables (DIM_SUBSCRIBERS 385,889; UCONNECT_MAY_MERGE uConnect-only 385,895) is 5,120 rows — past the 15-row tolerance. This is the same ~5,120 spread seen in yesterday's run, suggesting a stable systematic difference between the usage-details view and the other two tables rather than a growing data-quality issue — still worth a root-cause look since it has persisted two days running.
Duplicate checks are clean: 6 duplicated ACCOUNT_NUMBERs (12 rows) and 9 duplicated ICCIDs (44 rows) among active uConnect-only records — both well under the 100 threshold, unchanged from yesterday.
MTD terminations (21, covering 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-03) are below the threshold of baseline + 500 (2,800.0 + 500 = 3,300.0) — flags RED per the rule.

Known data-shape caveat (same as prior runs): termination dates are batch-applied, not day-by-day. Full-calendar-month check: July 2026 has 84,801 uConnect terminations total vs only 1,892 in its first 3 days; June 2026 has 72,485 total, and within just the first 3 days of June, 2,440 of those landed on 2026-06-03 alone in a single batch. August is already at 4,257 total (across dates recorded so far) vs only 21 in the first 3 days. Treat this RED with that batching context rather than as a standalone outage signal.
